o: Have preganglionic cell bodies at T5–T8

Their preganglionic cells are at T1 (and T2).
They ascend in the sympathetic trunk.
Relay in the ciliary ganglion

They relay in the superior cervical ganglion.
They pass through the ciliary ganglion without synapsing.
Reach the eye in the oculomotor nerve

They reach the eye mainly through the nasociliary and long ciliary nerves.
They travel up on the internal carotid artery first.
Follow the internal carotid artery as postganglionic fibres

Postganglionic fibres form the internal carotid plexus.
From it they spread to the branches of the artery and nearby nerves.
Receives preganglionic sympathetic fibres directly

Its cells are like postganglionic neurons, so fibres reach it without a relay.
They come in the splanchnic nerves.
Receives postganglionic sympathetic fibres

Fibres reaching it are preganglionic.
The medullary cells take the place of the postganglionic neuron.
Is controlled mainly by parasympathetic fibres

Its secretion is controlled by sympathetic fibres.
There is no significant parasympathetic control.
Develops from mesoderm

It develops from neural crest.
The cortex develops from mesoderm.
Has its sacral outflow from S1–3

The sacral outflow is from S2–4, in the pelvic splanchnic nerves.
They supply the hindgut and pelvic viscera.
Supplies the hindgut through the vagus

The vagus supplies the gut as far as about two-thirds of the transverse colon.
The pelvic splanchnic nerves supply the hindgut.
Has a cranial outflow in the trigeminal nerve

The cranial outflow is in III, VII, IX and X.
Postganglionic fibres may travel with branches of V.
Has ganglia near or in the organs supplied

Parasympathetic ganglia lie close to or within the target organ.
So preganglionic fibres are long, postganglionic short.
The greater splanchnic nerve comes from T5–9

It arises from the thoracic ganglia of T5–9.
It ends in the coeliac ganglia.
Their fibres relay in the sympathetic trunk ganglia

Splanchnic fibres pass through the trunk ganglia without relaying.
They relay in the coeliac and other prevertebral ganglia.
They pierce the central tendon of the diaphragm

They pierce the crura.
The vena cava goes through the central tendon.
The least splanchnic nerve comes from T10–11

The least splanchnic comes from T12; the lesser from T10–11.
The least ends in the renal plexus.
Sweat glands are supplied by parasympathetic fibres

Sweat glands receive only sympathetic fibres.
There is no parasympathetic supply to the skin.
Sweat glands have sympathetic cholinergic postganglionic fibres

Most sympathetic postganglionic fibres release noradrenaline, but those to sweat glands release acetylcholine.
This is a classic exception.
Sympathetic fibres reach the skin through white rami at every level

White rami exist only at T1–L2.
Fibres reach other levels by travelling in the trunk.
Every spinal nerve receives a grey ramus

Grey rami carry postganglionic fibres to all spinal nerves.
So every dermatome gets a sympathetic supply.
Travel with sympathetic nerves

Pain afferents mostly travel with sympathetic fibres.
They enter the cord through the white rami.
Travel with parasympathetic nerves

Many reflex afferents travel in the vagus and pelvic splanchnic nerves.
Most are not consciously perceived.
Have their cell bodies in the dorsal root ganglia or cranial sensory ganglia

Like somatic afferents, their cell bodies lie in sensory ganglia.
There is no relay in autonomic ganglia.
Explain referred pain by converging on the same cord segment as somatic fibres

Visceral and somatic fibres converge on the same dorsal horn neurons.
The brain wrongly locates the pain in the skin.
